body:
In article <31DB4B99.5729@philly.infi.net>, ltodd@philly.infi.net says...
>
>Here's a few quotes from some sick subversives who advocate overthrowing 
>the gov't.
>
>  "Mankind are disposed to suffer, while evils are sufferable, rthan to 
>right themselves by abolishing the forms to which they are accustomed. 
>But when a long train of abuses and usurpations, pursuing invariable the 
>same object, evinces a design to reduce them under absolute despotism, it 
>is their right, it is their duty, to throw off such government..."
>  --THE DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE
>
>  "We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system." -- 
> THE UNABOMBER MANIFESTO

Now you really have gone over the bend.  Do you really think that that the 
founders of this country are comparable to the Unabomber?

The signers of the declaration of independence signed their names (not 
fictional names like FC - or Anon) at great personal risk and fought for the 
freedom to produce without having an unelected dictatorial government 
confiscate their production.  This country was founded based upon a desire to 
achieve - by men and women who sacrificed everything so that their children 
would have a better life.  The imigrants that founded this country were the 
greatest entrepreneurs of all time.  In most cases, they gave up everything 
that they had, said goodbye to everyone that they had ever known, to make a 
dangerous journey to a foreign continent, where the only thing that anyone 
gave them was the freedom to work themselves to death so that their children 
could have a better life.

Teddy boy, on the other hand, lived in a shack, scribbled anonymous 
manifestos and blew up innocent people.  I don't know how to tell you this, 
but Ted was not fighting for a cause.  He blew people up because he was a 
psychotic serial killer.  The "manifesto" was just a pathetic attempt to 
justify his actions.

If you want to make an accurate comparison, compare Ted with Jeffrey Dammer 
or any other psychotic murderer.
